facts.fact: 灯灭之后，一群人夜里变成「幽灵」，游荡在 chaperones 每天早晨领他们走过的同一些环形走廊里。
facts.anchor: Then we became ghosts of the night, haunting those same circular hallways our chaperones led us down each morning.

facts.fact: 他们没有真正逃走所需的门卡，只能漂浮观望；等到感觉该看下一集时，就下坡到 therapy room，在地毯上坐好听新一集。
facts.anchor: We lacked the key cards necessary for true escape. So we floated and observed, until eventually we sensed it was time for another episode.

facts.fact: 那些夜晚，朋友会穿过双开门出场，手拿手电筒坐到巨型地下室活动室的前排，开口叙述另一集。
facts.anchor: My friend would emerge on those nights through the double doors and take their seat at the front of the massive basement rec room, flashlight in hand.

facts.fact: 朋友在字面意义上「被闹鬼」：他们完全清楚坐在地毯上的所有人都是幽灵，自己只是对一个满是幽灵的房间说话的又一个幽灵。
facts.anchor: Haunted in the literal sense of the word, because they knew perfectly well that all of us down there on the carpet were ghosts. That they were just one apparition speaking to a room full of others.

facts.fact: 叙述者关心的已不是下一集剧情而是私人问题：朋友为何如此急切地想把脑中的假电视节目掏出来，以至于几乎自杀。
facts.anchor: And why had my friend been so desperate to get theirs out that they had almost taken their own life?

facts.fact: 叙述者怀疑故事有自传成分：朋友把角色命名为 David Sawyer，可能正是以自己为名。
facts.anchor: Were parts of their story autobiographical? Was that why my friend had decided to name the character David Sawyer after themself?

facts.fact: 剧集里零星提到「the hospital」——Bethany 十几岁时被送进的那家可怕机构；叙述者怀疑那暗指的就是 Saint Thomas 本身。
facts.anchor: And what about those stray references to “the hospital,” to that dreadful place where Bethany had been committed as a teenager?

facts.fact: 朋友白天保持安静内敛，假装每晚讲给大家的故事根本不存在；叙述者也从未问出那些问题，觉得那样不敬甚至危险。
facts.anchor: They remained quiet and reserved in the daylight. They pretended as if those stories they told us each night didn’t even exist.
